title: Linking through student ID
description: Student ID is transmitted as part of the data flow, enabling linking of data to specific individuals across the system.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of student ID, course, and file reference can serve as quasi-identifiers that may link data to specific individuals.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The flow processes identified data including student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role.

title: Processing of unique identifier
description: Student ID is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, transmitted in the data flow.

title: Quasi-identifier in data flow
description: The combination of student ID, course, and file reference constitutes quasi-identifiers that can identify data subjects.

title: Detecting through observed communications
description: The data flow itself can be observed, potentially revealing information about student submissions and grading requests.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Student ID and file reference may be more sensitive than functionally required for routing the request.

title: Data propagation to other service
description: Personal data is propagated from the Grades Portal to the Assignment & Grading Service where it may not be strictly needed.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (Assignment & Grading Service) beyond what may be necessary.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be aware that their submission and grading data is being transmitted to the Assignment & Grading Service.

title: Lack of control over data sharing
description: Students may lack control over how their personal data is shared between the portal and grading service.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The flow may process more personal data than functionally needed for routing the submission and grading request.

title: Teacher identity linked through unique login identifier
description: Teacher logs in using a unique identifier (username/email) that links their identity to the submission queue they access, potentially enabling tracking of their review activities across sessions.
assumptions: Login credentials are unique and persistent across sessions

title: Quasi-identifiers in submission queue data
description: Submission queue data may contain combinations of attributes (course name, submission date, assignment type) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to link submissions to specific students or teachers.
assumptions: Submission metadata includes identifiable course and timing information

title: Processing of identified teacher and student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified information including teacher identity and student submission data, which are directly linked to specific individuals.
assumptions: System stores and processes personally identifiable information

title: Unique identifiers in submission records
description: Submission records contain unique references (student IDs, submission IDs) that identify the data subjects (students) whose work is being reviewed.
assumptions: Student submissions are tagged with unique identifiers

title: Potentially sensitive data types collected
description: The system may collect submission content and metadata that could be perceived as highly sensitive (e.g., academic performance data, potentially revealing personal circumstances).
assumptions: Submission data may include content that reveals personal or sensitive information

title: Unnecessary data analysis and enrichment
description: Submission data may be analyzed, enriched, or processed beyond what is functionally needed for the core task of reviewing submissions (e.g., pattern analysis, performance tracking).
assumptions: System may perform additional analytics on submission data

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Submission data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., administrators, other teachers, support staff) beyond the reviewing teacher.
assumptions: Multiple system roles have access to submission data

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data is being processed, stored, and potentially analyzed by the Grades Portal system.
assumptions: Students are not explicitly informed about all data processing activities

title: Limited data subject control over preferences
description: Students may lack control over how their submission data is processed, stored, or shared, with limited ability to set preferences or opt-out.
assumptions: No granular consent or preference mechanisms exist for submission data

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than is actually needed for the functional goal of reviewing submissions (e.g., collecting metadata beyond what's necessary for grading).
assumptions: Data collection scope exceeds functional requirements

title: Potential invalid consent for data processing
description: Student submission data processing may not rely on valid consent, particularly if students are required to submit work without explicit consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be unclear or absent for academic submission processing

title: Linking through student name identifier
description: Student names in the submission data serve as unique identifiers that can link the work content and submission times to specific students within the school context.
assumptions: Student names are unique within the school system and can be used to identify individual students.

title: Quasi-identifier combination linking
description: The combination of student name, work content, and submission times creates a quasi-identifier set that can uniquely identify students even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes is sufficiently unique to identify individual students.

title: Profiling through work content analysis
description: Work content can be analyzed to profile student performance, learning patterns, or behavioral characteristics, potentially linking data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Teachers or systems may analyze work content for patterns that reveal information about the student.

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The system explicitly processes and displays identified student information including names, work content, and submission times.
assumptions: Student names are personally identifiable information that is being processed.

title: Student name as identifier
description: Student names serve as unique references to the identity of the data subject (student) in the submitted work data.
assumptions: Student names are unique identifiers within the school context.

title: Revealing attributes in submission data
description: Work content and submission times reveal attributes about the student's academic performance, timing patterns, and engagement level.
assumptions: The content and timing of submissions provide revealing information about the student.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Student names and work content are sensitive personal data that may be more sensitive than strictly required for grade portal functionality.
assumptions: Work content may contain sensitive academic or personal information beyond what's needed for grading.

title: Fine-grained data disclosure
description: The data disclosed includes granular details (specific work content, exact submission times) that may be more detailed than necessary for teacher review.
assumptions: Teachers may not need to see the exact submission time or full work content for grading purposes.

title: Predetermined party access
description: Student data is made accessible to teachers (predetermined set of parties), which is functionally necessary but still represents data disclosure.
assumptions: Teachers are the intended recipients of this data for grading purposes.

title: Student unawareness of data sharing
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data (including work content and submission times) is being displayed to teachers through the portal.
assumptions: Students may not have clear visibility into how their data is being shared and displayed.

title: Lack of student control over data processing
description: Students lack control over how their submission data is processed, displayed, and shared with teachers through the portal.
assumptions: Students cannot customize or opt-out of data sharing for grading purposes.

title: Data minimization principle violation
description: The system may process more personal data (full work content, exact submission times) than strictly necessary for the grading functionality.
assumptions: Full work content and precise timing may exceed what's needed for teachers to assign grades.

title: Potential invalid consent for data processing
description: Student data processing may not rely on valid consent, particularly if students are minors and parental consent is required.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms for student data sharing may be inadequate or unclear.

title: Linking through unique student identifier
description: Student grades and teacher feedback are linked to the student through their unique student ID or username, enabling identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Student accounts use unique identifiers

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The portal processes identified student data (grades and feedback) that can be directly associated with specific students.
assumptions: Student data is personally identifiable

title: Revealing academic attributes
description: Grades and teacher feedback reveal attributes about the student's academic performance, learning patterns, and capabilities.
assumptions: Academic performance data is considered personal information

title: Sensitive grade data disclosure
description: Grades are sensitive personal data that may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be disclosed when strictly required.
assumptions: Academic grades are considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: Grades and feedback may be further processed, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is functionally needed for displaying to the student.
assumptions: Additional processing of grade data may occur beyond display functionality
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if additional processing occurs beyond display

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of how their grades and feedback data are collected, processed, stored, or disclosed by the portal.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not adequately inform students about all data processing activities
uncertainty_note: Depends on quality of privacy notices and consent mechanisms

title: Lack of student control over preferences
description: Students may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their grades and feedback data are processed.
assumptions: Limited customization options for data processing preferences
uncertainty_note: Depends on system design and consent mechanisms

title: Limited rectification/erasure control
description: Students may lack control to rectify incorrect grade data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant.
assumptions: Data retention and correction mechanisms may be limited
uncertainty_note: Depends on implementation of data subject rights

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than actually needed for the functional goal of displaying grades and feedback.
assumptions: Data collection may exceed functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data collection scope vs. functional needs

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Student grades and feedback data may be stored longer than functionally needed.
assumptions: Data retention policies may exceed necessary duration

title: Linking through parent-child account identifiers
description: Parent account is linked to child account, enabling linking of parent's access to child's grades through unique identifier association
assumptions: Parent account and child account are linked in the system

title: Quasi-identifier combining parent-child relationship
description: Combination of parent identity and child grades can serve as quasi-identifier to link data across contexts
assumptions: Parent-child relationship is stored and can be used for linking

title: Processing of identified parent and child data
description: System processes identified information including parent account credentials and child's grades
assumptions: Parent account and child grades are personally identifiable information

title: Unique identifier in parent account
description: Parent account contains unique references to parent identity enabling identification
assumptions: Parent account has unique identifiers (username, email, etc.)

title: Sensitive grade data collection
description: Grades are sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for the login and grade viewing function
assumptions: Grades are considered sensitive educational data

title: Potential unnecessary data treatment
description: Grades may be analyzed, stored, or processed beyond what is needed for the parent to view their child's grades
assumptions: System may retain or analyze grade data beyond immediate viewing
uncertainty_note: Depends on system architecture and data retention policies

title: Child unawareness of grade access
description: Child data subject may not be aware that their grades are being accessed by parent through the portal
assumptions: Child is the data subject whose grades are being accessed

title: Limited parent control over data processing
description: Parent may have limited control over how their child's grade data is processed, stored, or shared
assumptions: Parent account settings may not provide granular control over data processing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: System may process more personal data than strictly needed for the grade viewing functionality
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle applies to educational data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data collection scope and necessity

title: Linking through unique identifiers in account records
description: Account records written to the directory contain unique identifiers (e.g., student IDs, account IDs) that can be used to link data across systems and contexts.
assumptions: Account records contain unique identifiers that persist across the system.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Account records may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., name, date of birth, course enrollment) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Account records contain multiple attributes that can be combined to identify individuals.

title: Processing of identified data in account records
description: The grading service processes and writes identified account records to the directory, making personal data directly identifiable.
assumptions: Account records contain personally identifiable information about students.

title: Processing of identifier data
description: Account records contain unique references to student identity that are written to the account directory.
assumptions: Account records include unique student identifiers.

title: Processing of quasi-identifier data
description: Account records may contain combinations of attributes that can uniquely identify students when combined.
assumptions: Account records include multiple attributes that can serve as quasi-identifiers.

title: Collection of sensitive data types beyond grading needs
description: Account records may contain more sensitive personal data than functionally required for the grading service's core functionality.
assumptions: Account records may include data beyond what is needed for assignment and grading.

title: Data propagation to other services
description: Account records written to the directory may be accessible by or propagated to other services where the data is not needed for grading purposes.
assumptions: The account directory is accessible by multiple services beyond the grading service.

title: Unawareness of data processing by students
description: Students may not be aware that their account records and parent-child relationship links are being written to the account directory by the grading service.
assumptions: Students are not informed about all data processing activities.

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Students may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their account data is processed and stored in the directory.
assumptions: No mechanism exists for students to control data processing preferences.

title: Lack of control over data rectification and erasure
description: Students may lack the ability to request correction or removal of their account records from the directory.
assumptions: No mechanism exists for students to request data rectification or erasure.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The grading service may process more personal data than is actually needed for assignment and grading functionality.
assumptions: Account records contain data beyond what is functionally required for grading.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Account records may be stored in the directory longer than functionally needed for grading purposes.
assumptions: No clear retention policy exists for account records in the directory.
